title: House edge and a single outcome
subtitle: Compare distributions, then choose independently.

theory.text: House edge is a long-run expectation under specified rules and decisions, not a prediction of your next session. In the fictional point models below, each entry is equally likely. The mean is the sum of the entries divided by their number. For example, −1, −1, +1 has mean −1/3, yet its next outcome can be +1. A positive sample does not remove a negative expectation. These are teaching distributions, not a numerical estimate of blackjack house edge; actual blackjack needs its exact rules, payouts and strategy.

theory.text: Expected value (EV) averages every possible outcome with its probability. Choose a decision using that whole distribution, not the last result. For example, [−2,+4] averages +1 and [−1,+1] averages 0. A shown −2 for the first model does not make the second model better. These fictional points have no monetary value. The displayed sample is a fixed illustration of one possible result, not a random experiment or an estimate of blackjack action EV.

theory.text: Variance measures the spread around the mean: average the squared distance of each outcome from that mean. [−1,+1] and [−3,+3] both have mean 0; their variances are 1 and 9. A larger variance does not imply a larger EV. With independent repeats the variance of the sum grows with the number of repeats; the variance of the average shrinks, but an individual outcome remains uncertain. Fixed examples below illustrate spread and do not prove that a losing run cannot happen.

Points are only a mathematical teaching device, not a bankroll or real game.
